lead: A static VAR compensator (SVC) is a shunt power-electronics circuit that changes reactive power in milliseconds to hold a bus voltage steady. It exists because transmission lines and loads need reactive power, called vars: too little leaves voltage low and limits power transfer; too much raises voltage. Thyristors switch reactors and capacitors quickly, with no mechanical breaker. SVCs sit at weak 33 kV, 132 kV and 400 kV buses, at HVDC terminals and near arc furnaces. The wider family, FACTS (flexible AC transmission systems), adds series and combined converters that raise line capacity and steer power flow.
prereq: You need Unit 5 for thyristor AC controllers, Unit 4 for voltage-source converters and Unit 2 for converter reactive-power demand; HVDC transmission shows where that var demand appears.

sections.h3: Why reactive power sets voltage and transfer

blocks.text: Reactive power Q, measured in var, kvar or MVar, is the power that swings between a magnetic field or an electric field and the source. It does no useful work, but it sets voltage. An inductive load draws lagging current and absorbs Q, so the line drops more voltage. A capacitor draws leading current and supplies Q, which raises voltage.

blocks.where: P is active power in watts (W); V_S and V_R are sending-end and receiving-end phase-to-phase voltages in volts (V); X is line series reactance in ohms (Ω); δ is the angle between the two voltages in radians. For small δ, P ≈ V_S V_R δ / X.

blocks.text: An SVC is a controlled shunt susceptance B_SVC. It injects reactive current I_Q = B_SVC V into the bus. B_SVC is in siemens (S); positive means leading current (capacitive) and negative means lagging current (inductive). The controller measures bus voltage and changes B_SVC so voltage returns to its set point. Response takes one or two cycles, far faster than a mechanical capacitor bank.
At a weak bus, this support raises V_R in the formula, so the same line carries more P.

sections.h3: TCR, TSC and the SVC characteristic

blocks.text: A thyristor-controlled reactor (TCR) is a fixed reactor L in series with two anti-parallel thyristors. The firing angle α is measured from the positive-going zero crossing of the bus voltage. At α = 90° the thyristors conduct for the whole half cycle; at α = 180° they do not conduct. The fundamental susceptance is:

blocks.where: B_L(α) is the fundamental susceptance of the TCR in siemens (S); α is the firing angle in radians, between π/2 and π; X_L = ωL is the reactor reactance in ohms (Ω); ω = 2πf is angular frequency in rad/s; L is inductance in henry (H).

blocks.text: With a fixed capacitor C in parallel, the SVC susceptance is B_SVC = B_C − B_L(α), where B_C = ωC. The TCR absorbs lagging vars and the capacitor supplies leading vars; the net is their difference. At α = 90° the TCR absorbs its maximum, so the SVC is at its most lagging setting. At α near 180° the TCR is off, so the capacitor makes the SVC leading.

items: TCR + fixed capacitor (TCR+FC): continuous control from leading to lagging within rating.
Thyristor-switched capacitor (TSC): capacitor connected in steps; leading vars only, no continuous control from one unit.
Thyristor-switched reactor (TSR): reactor connected in steps; lagging vars only.

blocks.text: The V-I characteristic shows the control range. Inside it, bus voltage stays nearly constant while reactive current changes. At the leading limit the SVC acts like a fixed capacitor, so its current falls when voltage falls. At the lagging limit it acts like a fixed reactor. The rating is the maximum continuous MVar at a stated bus voltage, with a short-time overload.

sections.h3: STATCOM, series devices and active filters

blocks.text: A STATCOM is a voltage-source converter (VSC) behind a coupling reactor. It controls the magnitude and phase of its AC output voltage. If the converter voltage is higher than the bus voltage, leading current flows and the STATCOM supplies vars; if lower, it absorbs vars. The converter can hold current up to its rating while the bus voltage sags, so its V-I curve is current-limited. An SVC of the same MVar rating gives less reactive current at low voltage because it behaves as a fixed susceptance. Unit 4 covers the VSC and its current control.

items: TCSC: a thyristor-controlled reactor in parallel with a series capacitor; it changes the line's effective series reactance, raising the transfer limit and damping oscillations.
SSSC: a series VSC injects a voltage in quadrature with line current; it behaves like a controllable series reactance.
UPFC: shunt and series converters share a DC link; the series converter controls line active and reactive power, while the shunt converter supplies active power and vars.

blocks.text: An active harmonic filter is a shunt VSC that measures the load current, extracts its harmonic components, and injects equal and opposite harmonic currents. The supply then sees a nearly sinusoidal current. The same converter can supply vars, so it also works as a STATCOM.

At an HVDC terminal, line-commutated converters absorb a large fraction of their active power as vars; see HVDC transmission. An SVC or STATCOM on the AC bus supplies those vars, holds the bus voltage and supports commutation after a fault.

figure.caption: The FACTS family: shunt devices inject current at a bus, series devices inject voltage in the line, and the UPFC combines both. The SVC branch is the one built from a TCR and fixed capacitor.

spec.aria: The FACTS family splits into shunt devices (SVC and STATCOM), series devices (TCSC and SSSC) and the combined UPFC.

examples.question: A 33 kV, 50 Hz bus has a TCR with reactor reactance X_L = 10 Ω per phase. The firing angle is α = 120°. Using B_L(α) = [2(π − α) + sin 2α] / (π X_L), find the fundamental TCR current per phase and the reactive power absorbed. Repeat for α = 90°.
steps: Convert α = 120° to radians: α = 120 × π / 180 = 2.094 rad. Then π − α = 3.142 − 2.094 = 1.047 rad, and 2α = 4.189 rad.
The phase voltage is V_phase = 33 kV / √3 = 19.05 kV = 19052 V.
The fundamental current is I = B_L V_phase = 0.0391 × 19052 = 745 A = 0.745 kA.
The three-phase reactive power is Q = √3 V_LL I = 1.732 × 33 kV × 0.745 kA = 42.6 MVAr.
examples.answer: At α = 120°, B_L = 0.0391 S, I = 0.745 kA and Q = 42.6 MVAr; at α = 90°, B_L = 0.1 S, I = 1.905 kA and Q = 108.9 MVAr.
examples.check:
import math
XL = 10.0
VLL = 33e3
def B(alpha):
    return (2*(math.pi - alpha) + math.sin(2*alpha)) / (math.pi*XL)
a1 = math.radians(120)
a2 = math.pi/2
B1 = B(a1)
B2 = B(a2)
Vph = VLL/math.sqrt(3)
I1 = B1*Vph
I2 = B2*Vph
Q1 = math.sqrt(3)*VLL*I1
Q2 = math.sqrt(3)*VLL*I2
print(round(B1,4))
print(round(I1/1000,3))
print(round(Q1/1e6,1))
print(round(B2,4))
print(round(I2/1000,3))
print(round(Q2/1e6,1))

traps: Taking the TCR output as the SVC output. The TCR only absorbs vars; the fixed capacitor supplies leading vars; the net SVC output is the difference B_C − B_L(α).
Putting α in degrees inside the formula. Convert to radians first. Also keep the sign of sin 2α: at α = 120°, sin 240° = −0.866, not +0.866.

Mixing SVC and STATCOM V-I behaviour. An SVC at its limit looks like a fixed susceptance, so current falls with voltage. A STATCOM holds current up to its limit, so it gives more reactive current at low voltage.
Calling a TSC continuously variable. A single TSC switches a capacitor in steps; continuous control needs a TCR or several TSC steps.
Treating UPFC as a shunt-only SVC. A UPFC has a shunt converter and a series converter, and the series converter is what controls line power flow.

quiz.q: What does SVC stand for, and what quantity does it control at the bus?
quiz.a: Static VAR Compensator; it controls bus voltage by injecting or absorbing reactive power (vars).

quiz.q: Why can a TCR plus fixed capacitor give continuous control when a TCR alone only absorbs vars?
quiz.a: The TCR absorbs a continuously adjustable lagging current. The fixed capacitor supplies a fixed leading current. The net SVC current is the difference, so the combination moves continuously between leading and lagging.

quiz.q: A TCR has X_L = 20 Ω. At α = 90°, find B_L and the reactive power at 11 kV phase-to-phase. Use I = B_L V_phase and Q = √3 V_LL I.
An SVC and a STATCOM have the same MVar rating at 1 pu voltage. The bus falls to 0.8 pu. Which gives more reactive current, and why?
quiz.a: The STATCOM. Its converter current stays near rated until the current limit. The SVC at its limit is a fixed susceptance, so its current falls roughly in proportion to voltage, to about 0.8 pu.

quiz.q: Name one series FACTS device and one combined FACTS device.
quiz.a: Series: TCSC or SSSC. Combined: UPFC.

quiz.q: What is the difference between a TSC and a TCSC?
quiz.a: A TSC is a shunt thyristor-switched capacitor used in an SVC for stepwise leading vars. A TCSC is a series thyristor-controlled capacitor that varies the line series reactance.

quiz.q: Why can an active harmonic filter replace a tuned passive filter in a plant with changing loads?
quiz.a: It measures the actual harmonic current and injects the opposite current, so it follows load changes and does not depend on a fixed tuning point. A passive filter is tuned to one frequency and can resonate if the load or network changes.

beyond: Not for the exam. Grid codes now ask wind and solar farms to provide voltage support like a STATCOM, so the same converter that exports power also injects vars. Research is moving from line-commutated HVDC to VSC-HVDC, where a converter can black-start a weak AC grid. Wide-bandgap SiC and GaN devices raise switching frequency and shrink the coupling reactor and filter. Search for FACTS, STATCOM, VSC-HVDC, active harmonic filter and grid-forming converter.
